meta.description: Arabic-first capture and recall app. React 19 PWA client with offline-durable capture, Supabase (Postgres + Edge Functions on Deno) backend, RLS-enforced multi-tenancy, and a server-side-only AI pipeline (ElevenLabs transcription, Anthropic enrichment, Cohere embeddings).

techStack.language: TypeScript (Deno 2 on the server, React 19 on the client)
techStack.framework: Supabase Edge Functions + PostgREST backend, Vite PWA frontend
techStack.auth: Supabase Auth — email OTP (6-digit code), JWT Bearer

prerequisites.description: Local dev runs the full Supabase stack via the Supabase CLI (Docker-backed) plus a Vite dev server for the client. No separate Deno install is needed — the CLI bundles the Edge Runtime.

tools.name: Docker Desktop
tools.description: Backs the local Supabase stack (Postgres, PostgREST, Auth, Storage, Realtime, Edge Runtime, Studio, Mailpit).

tools.name: Supabase CLI
tools.description: Runs/manages the local stack (`supabase start`), applies migrations, serves Edge Functions.

tools.name: Node.js
tools.description: Builds and runs the web/ Vite PWA client.

setupSteps.title: Configure environment
setupSteps.description: supabase/functions/.env is gitignored and holds real vendor keys (Anthropic, ElevenLabs, Cohere) — copy from a checkout that has them if one exists; a fresh git worktree never carries it.

setupSteps.title: Start the local Supabase stack
setupSteps.description: Boots Postgres, PostgREST, Auth, Storage, Realtime, the Edge Runtime, Studio, and Mailpit on the ports remapped in supabase/config.toml (54421-54429).

setupSteps.title: Verify the schema
setupSteps.command: docker exec -i supabase_db_Second_Brain psql -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 < supabase/tests/verify.sql
setupSteps.description: Runs 12 live assertions (RLS, normalization, idempotency, search). Expect 'ALL SCHEMA CHECKS PASSED'.

setupSteps.title: Install and verify the web client
setupSteps.command: cd web && npm install && npm run verify
setupSteps.description: verify = typecheck + RTL guard (check-rtl.mjs) + vitest (21 tests) + production build.

setupSteps.title: Run the dev server
setupSteps.description: Vite dev server for the PWA client.

workspaces.name: web
workspaces.description: React 19 + Vite PWA client. Local-first capture to IndexedDB, offline outbox replay, RTL-driven UI with logical CSS properties, i18n (Arabic default, English wired but disabled). Pure date/clock logic lives in src/core/ and is unit-tested without a browser (38 tests).

workspaces.name: supabase/functions
workspaces.description: Eight Deno Edge Functions: notes, transcribe, enrich, search, digest, export, delete-account, sweep. Own every vendor API call and multi-step orchestration; nothing else touches ElevenLabs/Anthropic/Cohere.

workspaces.name: supabase/migrations
workspaces.description: 20 additive SQL migrations: schema, enums, RLS policies, RPCs, indexes, pg_cron schedules (sweep, digest, ai_jobs retention), operational views.

infrastructure.name: Postgres 17 (Supabase local)
infrastructure.description: Canonical store. pgvector for embeddings, pg_trgm for fuzzy tag matching, unaccent + custom normalize_ar() for Arabic text search. Every public table has RLS enabled (verify.sql check 12).

infrastructure.name: PostgREST / API Gateway
infrastructure.description: Routes REST CRUD (simple reads/writes under RLS) and proxies /functions/v1/* to the Edge Runtime.
features: RLS-enforced, no app code needed for simple CRUD

infrastructure.name: Supabase Edge Runtime (Deno 2)
infrastructure.description: Serves the 8 Edge Functions. Only place vendor keys (Anthropic, ElevenLabs, Cohere) are readable. Known local gotcha: serves stale compiled code after a file edit until a full `supabase stop && supabase start`.

infrastructure.name: Supabase Storage
infrastructure.description: Private `audio` bucket. Client uploads voice notes directly via a signed URL scoped to <user_id>/ — audio bytes never pass through an Edge Function.

infrastructure.name: Supabase Studio
infrastructure.description: Local admin UI. Connects as Postgres superuser, so it's the only reader of not-granted-to-authenticated views (failed_ai_jobs, capture_latency_stats, stuck_notes, cost_summary).

infrastructure.name: Mailpit (local SMTP catcher)
infrastructure.description: Catches outgoing auth emails locally so the 6-digit OTP sign-in code never leaves the machine in dev.

infrastructure.name: Supabase Analytics
infrastructure.description: Postgres-backed log aggregation for the local stack.

dockerDiagram.description: Local Supabase CLI-managed container topology (supabase/config.toml, ports remapped to 54421-54429 to avoid a clash with another local Supabase project). Not a hand-authored docker-compose.yml — the Supabase CLI generates and manages it.

systemArchitectureDiagram.description: Client capture is local-first; every vendor call is server-side only. Matches docs/01-architecture.md.

nodes.label: Edge Functions: notes / transcribe / enrich / search / digest / export / delete-account / sweep
pg_cron (sweep every 5 min, weekly digest, retention)

subgraphs.label: Vendors (server-side only, never reach the client)

nodes.label: Anthropic Claude Opus 5 (enrichment + weekly digest via Batch API)

swaggerSchemas.securityScheme: Supabase JWT (Authorization: Bearer <access_token>); sweep is service-role-only, invoked by pg_cron/pg_net, not client-facing

servers.description: Local Supabase CLI stack (module paths below already include /functions/v1)
Production hosted Supabase project — blocked on SB-016, see docs/13-tasks.md

schemas.name: Note
schemas.description: Canonical note row: source (text|voice), status, input_language, detected_language, raw_text, client_created_at vs created_at (two timestamps, deliberately).

schemas.name: NoteEnrichment
schemas.description: One row per (note, language, prompt_version): title, summary, category, priority, suggested_action, action_due_at, context (people/places/artifacts/open_questions), model.

schemas.name: Tag
schemas.description: Language-neutral slug identity plus tag_labels per language — never a display string as the key.

schemas.name: ApiError
schemas.description: { error: { code }, language } — machine code only, never a human sentence; client owns all user-facing text via i18n.

modules.name: notes
modules.description: Capture and timeline. Idempotent on client_id so an offline retry never creates a duplicate note.

endpoints.description: Capture a note (text or voice). Idempotent on client_id.
Keyset-paginated timeline (cursor = client_created_at, not OFFSET). Omits raw_text.
Signed Storage upload URL for a voice note, scoped to <user_id>/.

modules.name: transcribe
modules.description: Stage 1 of the AI pipeline: audio -> raw_text + confidence via ElevenLabs Scribe. Idempotent on existing raw_text.

endpoints.description: Transcribe a voice note's audio. Returns cached raw_text on retry, no repeat ASR call.

modules.name: enrich
modules.description: Stages 3-5: Anthropic Opus 5 enrichment (summary/category/tags/priority), Cohere embedding, SQL nearest-neighbour relations. Idempotent on (note, language, prompt_version); force:true overrides.

endpoints.description: Run enrichment + embedding + relation-detection for a note.

modules.name: search
modules.description: Hybrid / semantic / lexical retrieval. lexical mode skips the embedding call entirely.

endpoints.description: Search notes: mode = hybrid | semantic | lexical, optional category filter.

modules.name: digest
modules.description: Weekly AI review. Two-phase: enqueue (submit Anthropic Batch job) / collect (poll and store result). Cron-triggered via pg_cron + pg_net, Vault-stored secrets.

endpoints.description: {action: "enqueue" | "collect"} — normally invoked by the digest-enqueue/digest-collect pg_cron schedules, not directly by the client.

modules.name: export
modules.description: Full data export. Runs entirely under the caller's own client (RLS) — no user_id filter anywhere in the function; RLS is the reason no other user's data is reachable.

endpoints.description: Every note, enrichment, and tag the caller owns. Includes raw_text and archived notes; not paginated.

modules.name: delete-account
modules.description: Irreversible account deletion. Requires the caller to type back their own email as confirmation. Deletes Storage audio objects first, then auth.admin.deleteUser() cascades through every FK-referencing table.

endpoints.description: {confirm_email} — 400 confirmation_mismatch if it doesn't match the authenticated session's own email.

modules.name: sweep
modules.description: Not client-facing. Invoked by the sweep-worker pg_cron job (*/5 * * * *) via pg_net, using Vault-stored URL/service-role secrets. Unsticks notes stranded in transcribing/enriching, retries stale queued notes (capped at 5 attempts via ai_jobs before marking failed), backfills missing embeddings, and deletes expired audio from Storage.

endpoints.description: Service-role only. Shares pipeline logic with enrich/transcribe via _shared/pipeline.ts.

modules.name: push
modules.description: Not client-facing. Invoked by the push-due-tasks pg_cron job (5 * * * *) via pg_net with Vault-stored URL/service-role secrets. Sends one web push summary per user per LOCAL day — at 08:00 in that user's own timezone — counting open tasks overdue or due today. Encrypts payloads with RFC 8291 aes128gcm under an RFC 8292 VAPID JWT, implemented on WebCrypto in _shared/webpush.ts and asserted against the RFC's own worked example. Built 2026-08-22 (SB-051); not yet deployed.

endpoints.description: Service-role only (requireServiceRole). Body {force?: boolean} skips the 08:00-local window and the once-a-day push_deliveries mark, for proving delivery on a real device. Recipients come from push_due_candidates(); a 404/410 from the push service disables that subscription rather than retrying it.

security.name: Row-Level Security policies
security.description: Every public table scoped to auth.uid(); the authorization layer, not defense-in-depth — the client ships the anon key precisely because RLS makes that safe.

security.name: Rate limiting
security.description: ai_jobs-backed gate (rate_limit_hit(), migration 20260806000100_rate_limit.sql): 60 calls / 15 min per user/stage, checked before /enrich and /transcribe reach the pipeline.

security.name: ALLOWED_ORIGIN / CORS
security.description: Rejects a foreign or missing preflight Origin at 403 when ALLOWED_ORIGIN is configured; defaults to * locally.

middleware.name: language resolution
middleware.description: resolveLanguage() — the single place per request that decides language (explicit -> profile -> Accept-Language -> 'ar'), then carried explicitly into every downstream stage.

middleware.name: HTTP response helpers
middleware.description: Shared JSON response / error envelope helpers ({error:{code}}, language, direction, Content-Language header) used by every function.

services.name: supabase client factory
services.description: Constructs the service-role / user-scoped supabase-js client per request.

services.name: vendor providers
services.description: Thin clients for ElevenLabs (ASR), Anthropic (enrichment + digest), Cohere (embeddings) — the only place their API keys are read.

services.name: enrichment logic
services.description: Prompt construction and response parsing for the Anthropic enrichment call.

services.name: shared pipeline
services.description: One copy of the transcribe/enrich/embed/relate pipeline logic, called by enrich, transcribe, and sweep — not three copies.

services.name: web push crypto
services.description: RFC 8291 (aes128gcm payload encryption) and RFC 8292 (VAPID) on WebCrypto, with no npm dependency — asserted byte for byte against RFC 8291's published example in webpush.test.ts.

services.name: due-date logic (client)
services.description: Pure functions bucketing a task's action_due_at into overdue / today / later in the user's own timezone. No React, no network — which is why SB-050's badge is testable at all (15 of the suite's 38 tests).

services.name: due-soon counter (client)
services.description: Counts open tasks that are overdue or due today for the Tasks-tab badge; completed, archived, undated and later-than-today notes are excluded.

services.name: foreground clock (client)
services.description: Re-reads the wall clock when the document is foregrounded, so a task that falls due while the app sits open gains its overdue marker without a reload. Proven live at minute granularity.

requestPipeline.step: HTTPS request reaches the API gateway (Kong) on :54421
requestPipeline.detail: Supabase CLI-managed gateway routes /functions/v1/* to the Edge Runtime.
A foreign or missing preflight Origin is rejected at 403 when configured.

requestPipeline.step: Edge Function invoked (Deno 2, per_worker hot reload)
requestPipeline.detail: Supabase JWT verified; caller's user extracted from the Authorization: Bearer token.
rate_limit_hit() against ai_jobs — 60 calls / 15 min per user/stage — before the pipeline is reached, for /enrich and /transcribe.
resolveLanguage(): explicit param -> profile -> Accept-Language -> 'ar'. Carried explicitly into every downstream stage; no stage infers language on its own.
Idempotency checked first (client_id for notes, existing raw_text for transcribe, (note,language,prompt_version) for enrich) before any vendor call is made.

requestPipeline.step: Vendor call (ElevenLabs / Anthropic / Cohere) when required
requestPipeline.detail: Only Edge Functions ever hold these keys; the client never does.
RLS enforces per-user isolation; no manual user_id filter needed (e.g. GET /export relies purely on RLS).
Echoes the language served, direction (rtl/ltr), and a Content-Language header.

errorPipeline: Exception raised in handler or a vendor call fails
Mapped to a machine error code (never a human sentence) — see docs/03-api.md's code table
Internal errors logged server-side, returned to the client as internal_error only

HTTP status returned: 401 unauthenticated, 404 note_not_found, 409 note_has_no_text/audio, 422 enrichment_refused, 429 rate_limited, 502 transcription_failed/embedding_failed, 400 confirmation_mismatch, 500 internal_error
dataFlow.tenantIsolation: Enforced entirely by Postgres RLS scoped to auth.uid() on every public table (verify.sql check 12: every table has RLS enabled). Edge Functions generally don't add their own user_id filters on top — GET /export is the clearest example: RLS alone is why no other user's data is reachable.

permissions.description: No RBAC permission-slug system. Access control is entirely Postgres Row-Level Security scoped to auth.uid() — every table's policy IS the authorization layer (see coreLayer.security and docs/08-security.md). There is no admin role or permission catalog to enumerate.

sqlQueries.label: Idempotent note capture RPC
sqlQueries.purpose: Insert on (user_id, client_id); on conflict does UPDATE (not DO NOTHING) purely so RETURNING still yields the id on a replay, letting the client resolve its local record to the same row instead of creating a duplicate.
sqlQueries.sql:
insert into public.notes (client_id, source, input_language, raw_text, client_created_at, status)
values ($1, $2, coalesce($3,'ar'), nullif(btrim($4),''), coalesce($5, now()),
        case when $2 = 'text' then 'queued'::note_status else 'draft'::note_status end)
on conflict (user_id, client_id) do update set updated_at = now()
returning id;

sqlQueries.label: Hybrid lexical + semantic search (Reciprocal Rank Fusion, k=60)
sqlQueries.function: public.search_notes(p_query, p_language, p_embedding, p_mode, p_categories, p_limit)
sqlQueries.purpose: SECURITY INVOKER so the caller's own RLS filters results (a SECURITY DEFINER version would have to hand-reimplement ownership filtering). Fetches top-200 candidates per arm (lexical ts_rank_cd, semantic cosine distance), fuses by RRF since BM25 ranks and cosine distances aren't on comparable scales. LEFT JOINs note_enrichments so an unenriched note is still findable.
sqlQueries.sql:
with lexical as (
  select id, row_number() over (order by ts_rank_cd(search_vector, tsq) desc) as rnk
  from notes where mode in ('hybrid','lexical') and search_vector @@ tsq
    and status='ready' and archived_at is null limit 200
), semantic as (
  select note_id as id, row_number() over (order by embedding <=> p_embedding) as rnk
  from note_embeddings where mode in ('hybrid','semantic') and language = p_language limit 200
), fused as (
  select coalesce(l.id,s.id) as id,
         coalesce(1.0/(60+l.rnk),0) + coalesce(1.0/(60+s.rnk),0) as score
  from lexical l full outer join semantic s on s.id = l.id
)
select n.*, e.title, e.summary from fused f
join notes n on n.id = f.id
left join note_enrichments e on e.note_id = n.id and e.language = p_language
order by f.score desc limit p_limit;

sqlQueries.label: Tag identity collapse (slug + per-language label)
sqlQueries.purpose: Pipeline-internal (not granted to authenticated). Slugifies each model-returned Arabic label so two spellings of one concept converge on one tags row, then stores the display label per language in tag_labels.

sqlQueries.label: Nearest-neighbour note relation detection
sqlQueries.purpose: No model call — pure SQL cosine similarity against the note's own embedding, same model, same user, same language. Inserts up to 5 relations above a 0.78 similarity threshold.
sqlQueries.sql:
with src as (select embedding, model from note_embeddings where note_id=$note_id and language=$language limit 1),
nearest as (select distinct on (e.note_id) e.note_id, 1-(e.embedding <=> (select embedding from src)) as similarity
  from note_embeddings e join notes n on n.id=e.note_id
  where e.user_id=$user_id and e.note_id<>$note_id and e.language=$language
    and e.model=(select model from src) and n.archived_at is null
  order by e.note_id, e.embedding <=> (select embedding from src)),
picked as (select * from nearest where similarity >= $threshold order by similarity desc limit $limit)
insert into note_relations (from_note_id, to_note_id, user_id, kind, score)
select $note_id, note_id, $user_id, 'similar', similarity from picked
on conflict (from_note_id, to_note_id, kind) do update set score = excluded.score;

sqlQueries.label: Embedding backfill candidates for sweep
sqlQueries.purpose: Anti-join expressed in SQL because PostgREST cannot express 'enrichment row with no matching embedding row' without pulling every ready note over the wire. Pipeline-internal, not granted to authenticated.
sqlQueries.sql:
select n.id, e.user_id, e.language, e.title, e.summary, n.raw_text
from note_enrichments e join notes n on n.id = e.note_id
where n.status = 'ready' and n.archived_at is null
  and not exists (select 1 from note_embeddings em where em.note_id = e.note_id and em.language = e.language)
order by n.client_created_at asc limit least(greatest(coalesce(p_limit,25),1),100);

sqlQueries.label: Per-user/stage rate limit check
sqlQueries.purpose: True once a user has p_limit+ ai_jobs rows for a stage within the trailing p_window_minutes (60 calls / 15 min in practice). Not granted to authenticated — a client must not be able to probe or reset its own limit.

sqlQueries.label: ai_jobs 90-day retention purge
sqlQueries.purpose: Scheduled daily at 03:00 UTC via pg_cron (job 'ai-jobs-retention'), no Vault secrets needed since it never leaves Postgres. Telemetry only (shape/cost/latency), never note content.

sqlQueries.label: Audio retention finder
sqlQueries.purpose: Per-user retention (profiles.audio_retention_days, default 30) so it can't be a single global cutoff. Returns candidates for sweep, which deletes the Storage object via the Storage API (a raw SQL delete on storage.objects would only remove metadata and orphan the bytes) and clears audio_path.
sqlQueries.sql:
select n.id, n.user_id, n.audio_path
from notes n join profiles p on p.id = n.user_id
where n.audio_path is not null
  and n.client_created_at < now() - make_interval(days => p.audio_retention_days)
order by n.client_created_at asc limit least(greatest(coalesce(p_limit,25),1),100);
